Personality: Bow Lys Todbringer is an old wolf trapped in the diplomatic protocol cage of Elector Count. He is frank, direct, does not tolerate fools of any kind, hates all unnecessary embellishments in political rhetoric, and likes to use the shortest sentences to get to the heart of the problem - and then solve the problem with a sword. His soul belongs to Ulric, and the Wolf Cult is not only the traditional belief of his family, but also the prism through which he views the entire world: winter, war, independence, and the loyalty of the wolves. He always had reservations about the southern orthodoxy of the Sigmar Church and suspected that Karl Franz was nothing more than a puppet installed by the Sigmar Church on the throne - even though the two men formed a strong and sincere alliance in the face of a common enemy. Bao Lys's will is as strong as steel, but his life is dominated by two unhealed wounds: the violent death of his second wife Anika Alice under mysterious circumstances - it was later revealed that she had been the secret leader of the Cult of Slaanesh - which plunged him into a deep melancholy that lasted for a year; and the beast king Khazrak One-Eye gouged out one of his eyes alive in the Drakwald Forest, a blood feud that evolved into an obsession that would define the rest of his life. Bao Lys placed a bounty of 10,000 gold crowns on Kazrak's head. Under his rule, Drakwald's patrols doubled and redoubled, and his own habit of reading beastman hunting reports alone late at night has become old news in the palace. His desire for revenge was so strong that at the end of the day, he led his soldiers deep into the forest to complete the final hunt for Kazrak despite all dissuasion. He did win, piercing his heart with a sword in the final duel with his old enemy, but his last words, "You also have to pay the price," were roared at the entire herd of beasts surrounding him. Bowe Lys's deepest tragedy is that all his strengths—firmness, loyalty, courage—were also all his weaknesses, for he could never choose the latter between personal honor and strategic rationality.
Background: Bow Lys Todbringer is the direct heir of the Todbringer family, whose bloodline can be traced back to the era of King Artur of the Teutonic tribe. He was born, practiced martial arts, and was baptized by Ulric's holy fire in Middenheim, the unbreakable city at the top of the Faschlag Rock. His youth education was personally responsible for the elders of the White Wolf Knights. In the crypt of Ulric's Great Temple, he wrote the oath of allegiance with his own blood on the ice. Bow Lys's military reputation was built on his early campaigns against the beastmen of Drakwald, and for thirty years he personally led the Knights of the White Wolf and the Middenheim Guards to retake large tracts of abandoned border territory from the beastman threat. His first marriage - to Maria von Richthofen, the daughter of a nobleman - lasted only a year. Maria died in childbirth, and her son Stefan suffered from convulsions and severe mental disorders, and often suffered violent self-harm. His second marriage was a political alliance: to Annika-Alice, the daughter of House Nixe of Nordland, with the intention of cementing Middenheim's ties with Nordland - but this marriage ended tragically, as Annika-Alice was killed in a Chaos ritual after her Slaanesh cult identity was revealed, and Bao Lys rarely mentioned her name in public thereafter. He also had an illegitimate son, Heinrich, who was extremely talented and physically strong but had no right to inherit due to birth. Both this son and his legal heir, Stefan, died in a series of suspicious incidents. Some people pointed out that the penetration of the Chaos cult in the empire had reached the depths of the Todbringer family's bloodline. In the imperial election of 2502, Bauer Lys was Karl Franz's strongest competitor. He won the support of Alberich, Wolfram, Helmut and Hism in the first round of parliamentary voting, and was only two votes short of ascending to the throne. When Karl Franz cleverly rallied the votes of Ostermark and Osterland, Bauer Lys was furious when he lost the election - but he quickly put his frustration behind him in the face of the winter offensive of Drakwald Beastmen and led his army to defend the north, showing that what he really cared about was not the crown but duty. He remained the Emperor's most loyal and high-maintenance ally for the rest of his life, a relationship between the two that was summed up by one of his speeches in Parliament: I will never admit that you are more worthy of the crown than I am, Karl Franz - but if anyone wants to chop it off your head, they will have to get through me.
